title: The Original Way
subtitle: A Pilgrim's Guide to the Camino Primitivo
description_short: An honest guide to the Camino Primitivo: fourteen walking days from Oviedo over the mountains of Asturias to Santiago, the high variant, when to go, what to carry and how to arrive.
description_long:
The Camino Primitivo is the Original Way: about 320 km from the old Asturian capital of Oviedo over the mountains of western Asturias, across a pass of about 1,030 m into Galicia, past the Roman walls of Lugo, and at Melide onto the last stretch of the Camino Francés to the cathedral of Santiago de Compostela. It is said to follow the road of King Alfonso II in the ninth century, and it is known as the demanding Way.

This guide is written for the Planner first and the Walker's evenings second. It is plain about the difficulty, and it helps you decide whether the mountains are your Camino, shape the walk, pack, and know what to check locally. It explains the choice between the high Hospitales route and the lower road by Pola de Allande, says what the official sources say about them, and tells you to check conditions before you go. It states the Pilgrim's Office rules for the Compostela as the Office writes them.

You will find the walk in fourteen days by region, Asturias, the border and the high hills of Lugo, and Galicia, with other ways to split them; chapters on when to go, on sleeping, eating and resting, on body, weather and safety (written with extra care for this road), on the inner side of walking, and on arriving in Santiago and going home.

Every distance is marked approximate, and the book says where sources differ. It names no hostels, cafes or prices, because they change; it sends you to the CaminoPlus app and to local information for the live answer. Its facts come from named public sources, which the book credits.
